arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Alaska's counsel argued the statehood act is insufficient. He cited the Idaho case principles. He emphasized the need for explicit ratification.
The United States counsel argued for federal retention. He referenced the Glacier Bay context. He disputed the adequacy of Alaska's showing.
Justices questioned the clarity of congressional intent. They probed the relationship between park status and land title. They examined the specific statutory language.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests state ownership of underwater lands. The dispute centers on Glacier Bay National Park. Alaska seeks title to these submerged areas. The federal government asserts it kept them.
